fed.stage_b_mechanics:
Stage B (PRs #1139–#1180) federates five decision-facing ledgers by threading shared axes through each store's existing file — no store is migrated or replaced. The one-grader law is enforced: every ledger calls engine.grading.forward_metrics (engine/grading.py:175) for all horizons in one pass rather than per-horizon helpers, so fill convention and window arithmetic are identical across stores.

The one shared grader module is engine/grading.py. Its __all__ (lines 77–93) exports the complete shared vocabulary:

SPINE_HORIZONS = (5, 10, 21, 63, 126) — the fwd_mfe horizon set (grading.py:140).
fwd_mfe_{H} columns — max favorable excursion per horizon from forward_metrics() (grading.py:181–238).
TerminalState constants — STOPPED / DEAD_MONEY / CUSHIONED / CLEAN_LIFTOFF (grading.py:253–262); barrier constants STOP_BARRIER=0.95, CUSHION_BARRIER=1.05, LIFTOFF_15=1.15, LIFTOFF_8=1.08, LIFTOFF_HORIZON_126=126, LIFTOFF_HORIZON_21=21 (grading.py:129–134) are imported by every store so definitions are shared even when the fill path differs (CN T+1 HL2 vs US next-bar).
terminal_state_clean15_126, terminal_state_clean8_21, post_cushion_breach — the per-fire partition columns written by every store.
Regime stamp keys from _REGIME_STAMP_KEYS (qledger.py:246–249): rate_pressure, quad_hard_label, fused_risk_label, vol_regime, risk_radar_state, regime_vector_degraded, vector_asof, staleness_hours. US stamp is primary on all US-lane stores. HK/CA/CN stores prefix us_* and set own_market_regime=null with a documented constraint (no PIT-append HK/CA/CN regime history exists yet). track_record.py IDENTITY_COLS (lines 101–114) lists the exact column spelling.
species_id / archetype — nullable on all stores; non-null only where species_registry.json has an unambiguous one-to-one binding to that ledger.

The five federated stores and their per-store fill rules:
1. engine/track_record.py (Stage B-a, PR #1139): US next-bar fill via grading.fill_index; store at data/track_record/ (gitignored-local). Key (ticker, date, type).
2. scripts/grade_us_board.py (Stage B-b, PR #1142): pre-computed retro_grades.parquet at data/us_board_ledger/retro_grades.parquet (77 KB); already next-bar-filled and excess-vs-SPY graded; read by spine.adapt_us_board (spine.py:255).
3. engine/board_ledger.py (Stage B-c, PR #1147): HK/CA boards; grading.fill_index for next-bar convention; suspended rows (no valid print within 5 sessions) keep spine cols null — suspension rule is the HK-native fill rule preserved per-store.
4. engine/china_standout_track.py (Stage B-d, PR #1151): CN T+1 HL2 fill (locked-limit-excluded rows get null spine axes); barrier constants imported from engine.grading but applied on the CN-native fill path; fill_basis="t1_hl2" provenance column on every row.
5. engine/qledger.py (Stage B-e, PR #1180): register_batch() stamps regime vector at claim time (qledger.py:314–324); stores species_id=null/archetype=null by default; grader appends fill_convention="next_bar" + entry_fill_date on every grade row (qledger.py:555, 747).

The shared schema is defined in engine/grading.py (SPINE_HORIZONS, TerminalState constants, barrier values) and engine/track_record.py (IDENTITY_COLS and MATURATION_COLS column lists with comments). engine/board_ledger.py:168–190 and engine/china_standout_track.py:119–151 show the per-store column lists that must be a superset of the shared axes. qledger.py:246–249 holds _REGIME_STAMP_KEYS. spine.py:COLUMNS (lines 84–90) is the read-side canonical schema for the materialized parquet index.
fed.qledger_adapter:
The existing qledger→spine adapter is engine/spine.py:adapt_desk_scorer (lines 347–392) for the desk_scorer family of qualitative desks. It maps each desk's scored.jsonl (7 desks listed in _DESK_SCORED, lines 334–343: ai_desk, policy_intent, radar, stock_desk, demand_chain, narrative_brain, thematic_desk) into SpinePrediction rows with family="desk:{name}", horizon=63, direction=1, size_binding=False, universe="desks". Hit/miss verdicts become outcome_excess= ±|realized| with sign encoding. The key join via signal_id="desk:{name}:{sid}".

This adapter maps ONLY the desk scorer's scored.jsonl rows — the qualitative desk verdict layer. It does NOT adapt the qledger's own claims.jsonl + grades.jsonl directly into the spine. The qledger's grade rows carry a different schema: {claim_id, horizon_d, excess, hit, bench_ret, control_ret, fill_convention, entry_fill_date} keyed by claim_id (qledger.py:680–750). The spine SpinePrediction rows carry {signal_id, engine, family, as_of, symbol, horizon, score, direction, outcome_excess, outcome_graded} (spine.py:COLUMNS lines 84–90).

The mapping between the two schemas: qledger claim_id is the qledger's stable identifier (desk|asof|scope_key|horizon_d|direction hash, qledger.py:129–134), while spine.signal_id for desk scorer rows uses "{engine}:{as_of}:{symbol}:{horizon}" (spine.py:14). The join key for a W2 query layer would be (as_of / asof, symbol / scope.key, horizon_d / horizon, desk / engine) — there is no single foreign key today bridging claims.jsonl rows to spine predictions.parquet rows.

Limits: (1) The adapt_desk_scorer adapter covers only the 7 desks in _DESK_SCORED; the claims from backfill_qledger_us.py (altdata, radar, policy desks) and backfill_qledger_intel_hub.py are NOT adapted into the spine — they live only in claims.jsonl/grades.jsonl. (2) qledger grades at horizons {5,21,63} (GRADE_HORIZONS, qledger.py:87) while the spine's SPINE_HORIZONS are (5,10,21,63,126) — no 10d or 126d grade row exists in qledger. (3) qledger does NOT write fwd_mfe_* or terminal_state_* columns — those Stage B axes exist only in the five parquet/jsonl stores above, not in qledger grades. (4) qledger's entry anchor is next_bar (post Stage B-e) but older rows carry fill_convention="asof_legacy" (qledger.py:555, 593) — a documented discontinuity.
fed.query_requirements:
A W2 query layer answering "what did engine X claim in regime Y at horizon H, and what happened" needs:

JOIN KEYS PER LEDGER
- spine (data/spine/predictions.parquet): primary key signal_id; join fields: engine, family, as_of (date str), symbol, horizon (int), direction.
- track_record (data/track_record/track_record.parquet, gitignored-local): key (ticker, date, type); join via (ticker≡symbol, date≡as_of, horizon from _SPINE_HORIZONS (5,10,21,63,126)).
- us_board_ledger/retro_grades.parquet (77 KB): key (as_of, lane, ticker, horizon); already adapted into spine via adapt_us_board — no additional join needed if spine is kept current.
- board_ledger (data/board_ledger/{hk,ca}_board.parquet): key (date≡as_of, ticker≡symbol); spine cols are in the parquet directly post Stage B-c; query layer reads these directly.
- china_standout_track: key (date≡as_of, ticker≡symbol); fill_basis="t1_hl2" must be preserved as a partition column so cross-market readers never conflate CN fills with US/HK fills.
- qledger claims/grades (data/qledger/claims.jsonl 7,937 rows/4.3 MB + grades.jsonl 617 KB): join key claim_id bridges claims→grades; join to other ledgers requires (asof≡as_of, scope.key≡symbol, horizon_d≡horizon, desk≡engine-family). No direct foreign key today.
- forward_logs (china_sector_cycles 20 KB, sector_cycles 18 KB, country_cycles 13 KB, market_state 948 B, risk_radar 4.1 KB): these carry aggregate/sector-level claims not per-ticker; query layer must handle scope_type=sector/basket/macro in addition to entity.

HORIZON NORMALIZATION
- Spine SPINE_HORIZONS: (5, 10, 21, 63, 126) — trading days (grading.py:140).
- qledger GRADE_HORIZONS: (5, 21, 63) — calendar days but with next-bar fill convention; the 21d and 63d are comparable to spine's 21/63 after the Stage B-e fill migration, but the missing 10d and 126d mean qledger rows cannot populate those cells. The W2 layer must mark qledger rows as horizon_coverage={5,21,63} and leave fwd_mfe_10, fwd_mfe_126, terminal_state_* null rather than fabricating values.
- track_record native horizons: 20/60/180 trading days (pre-Stage B maturation cols) plus the new SPINE_HORIZONS (5,10,21,63,126) post Stage B-a. The 20/60/180 columns do NOT map to spine horizons — the query layer must either drop them or expose them separately as track_record-native, never aliased as fwd_ret_21 or fwd_ret_63.
- CN T+1 HL2 fill: china_standout_track records fill_basis="t1_hl2"; the query layer must carry fill_basis as a first-class column and never aggregate CN rows with US/HK rows in a fill-convention-mixed pool.

OUTCOME VOCABULARY MAPPING
- Spine: outcome_excess = signed next-bar-filled forward excess return vs benchmark; direction encodes sign safety; outcome_graded=bool.
- qledger: excess = subject_ret − bench_ret; hit=bool|None (null for salience-only direction=0); state chip UNGRADED/ACCRUING/GRADED.
- track_record: outcome = win/loss/still_held; fwd_mdd_{20,60,180}; fwd_ret_{20,60,180}; fwd_mfe_{5,10,21,63,126}; terminal_state_clean15_126/clean8_21.
- Reconciliation: the query layer must expose outcome_excess (the common signed-excess vocabulary) as the canonical outcome column and carry provenance: outcome_source in {"spine_adapter","qledger_grade","track_record_maturation","board_ledger_grade","cn_track_maturation","forward_log_grade"}.
- Terminal state vocabulary is STOPPED/DEAD_MONEY/CUSHIONED/CLEAN_LIFTOFF from engine.grading.TerminalState (grading.py:253–262); exists only in track_record, board_ledger, and china_standout_track — not in qledger or spine proper.

PIT CONSTRAINTS
- Keep-FIRST per (as_of, symbol, ledger) is the universal PIT law (stated in board_ledger, china_standout_track, track_record docstrings). The query layer must enforce this on any cross-ledger union.
- qledger regime stamps are written at registration time from the persisted data/regime/regime_vector.parquet last-row-with-date≤asof (qledger.py:268–277) — PIT by design. track_record uses the same source. board_ledger and china_standout_track use get_vector_for_date on the same persisted file.
- own_market_regime is null for all HK/CA/CN rows today — a documented constraint, not a bug. The query layer must surface this nullity rather than silently forward-filling.
- The track_record parquet is gitignored-local (synapse.yml note line 831) — it will not be present in CI or on a fresh clone. The query layer must degrade to an empty frame for that store (consistent with the spine's degrade-never-raise law, spine.py:148).
- qledger discontinuity: grade rows before Stage B-e lack fill_convention and carry asof-bar fills (qledger.py:555, 686–687). The query layer must expose fill_convention per row, never silently pool next_bar and asof_legacy rows in the same IC calculation.
fed.recommendations:
Recommendation: materialized Parquet index, built by a new engine/neuralweb/query.py reader library that writes data/neuralweb/spine_index.parquet nightly as part of the engine lane (after grading, before render).

DESIGN

The W2 query layer is a two-part deliverable:
1. engine/neuralweb/query.py — a pure-read library (no imports from the nightly runner or render layers, mirroring the spine.py and neuralweb/read.py pattern). Public API: build_index(root) → pd.DataFrame; load_index(root) → pd.DataFrame; query(engine=None, regime=None, horizon=None, as_of_before=None) → pd.DataFrame. build_index runs all adapters, unions the five federated stores, and writes the materialized parquet. load_index reads it.

2. data/neuralweb/spine_index.parquet — the materialized cross-ledger index. Canonical columns (superset of spine.COLUMNS with provenance extensions):
   signal_id, engine, family, ledger (source enum), as_of, symbol, universe, horizon, direction, size_binding, fill_basis, score, outcome_excess, outcome_graded, graded_at, terminal_state_clean15_126, terminal_state_clean8_21, fwd_mfe_5, fwd_mfe_10, fwd_mfe_21, fwd_mfe_63, fwd_mfe_126, outcome_source, rate_pressure, quad_hard_label, fused_risk_label, vol_regime, risk_radar_state, vector_asof, species_id, archetype, event_key.

WHY MATERIALIZED PARQUET, NOT ON-DEMAND READER

An on-demand reader that unions five stores on every call costs O(file reads × callers). The qledger claims.jsonl is 4.3 MB JSONL (7,937 rows), grades.jsonl is 617 KB — both must be fully scanned and joined on every call. The spine/predictions.parquet is 33 KB; retro_grades is 77 KB; forward_logs are 10–20 KB each. Total raw data at today's scale: ~6 MB across six stores. At the current accrual rate (one year of daily rows across ~5 ledgers), the index reaches ~3–5 MB as parquet (columnar compression on repeated string columns is typically 5–10×). Materialized parquet: one read < 5 MB for any downstream consumer; on-demand union: 6 MB JSONL parse + 5 parquet reads on every N3/N4 call. The parquet wins.

REFRESH CADENCE

Nightly, in the engine lane, after scripts/grade_qledger.py and after the forward_log graders (the two jobs that advance outcome columns). Placement in daily.yml: after grade_qledger and grade_us_board steps, before scripts/build_reliability_kernel.py (W3). This matches the pattern of world_state.json (engine lane, engine/neuralweb/world_state.py) and spine.py's rebuild_from_adapters step.

LANE PLACEMENT

Engine lane (not render lane): the index is a graded-data artifact, not a display artifact. It writes to data/neuralweb/spine_index.parquet (git-tracked, mirroring spine/predictions.parquet). synapse.yml entry: owner_program=neural-web, producer=engine/neuralweb/query.py, cadence=daily-engine, tier=infrastructure, consumers={engine/neuralweb/reliability_kernel.py, engine/neuralweb/graph.py, engine/passport.py, engine/alert_triage.py}.

EXPECTED SIZE

At today's data: ~5–8 MB parquet (the qledger's 7,937 claims dominate; each other ledger contributes hundreds to low thousands of rows; columnar compression on the string regime columns and repeated engine/family values yields 5–10× compression on the ~6 MB raw total). At 3 years of daily accrual: ~15–25 MB. Fits in git (no R2 needed at this scale).

TRACK_RECORD GITIGNORED CAVEAT

The track_record parquet is gitignored-local (confirmed in synapse.yml). build_index must call adapt_track_record in a try/except that yields an empty frame on missing file, stamped in the index metadata so N3 can flag the cold-start cell. This matches the spine.py degrade-never-raise law (spine.py:148).

qi.w6_monitor_status:
The W6 promotion monitor lives in scripts/grade_qledger.py as a "POST-STEP" embedded in the nightly grading job (lines 14-30 of the module docstring, confirmed). It is ARMED: wired into scripts/collect.py (collect.py calls run_as_collect_step, which calls run_readiness_post_step after emit_ladder_states), and daily.yml:134-139 confirms the collect step runs nightly and stages site/qledger/track_record.json.

What it watches: after every nightly grade run it calls compute_promotion_readiness() over every family in config/qual_ladder.yml. It evaluates promotion_check() (§3 gate: n_dates>=25 independent clusters + Wilson CI lower bound > 0 vs matched control) at each of the three GRADE_HORIZONS (5/21/63d).
